albums.blurb: Mulatu Astatke, the vibraphonist and arranger known as the father of Ethio-jazz, studied in London and at Berklee (its first African student) before fusing Ethiopian pentatonic modes with jazz and Latin rhythm sections. Mulatu of Ethiopia, recorded in New York for Worthy Records after his two Afro-Latin Soul volumes, is the first full-length statement of that fusion: seven instrumentals built on vibraphone, saxophone, flute, and wah-wah guitar, with no vocals anywhere on the record.
albums.reception: Long out of print and traded as a collector's item, the album was given its first official reissue by Strut Records in 2017, which restored the original seven-track program alongside mono mixes.

albums.blurb: Weyes Blood is the project of Los Angeles songwriter Natalie Mering, who appears in Mark's library as co-vocalist on Drugdealer's The End of Comedy. Titanic Rising, her fifth studio album and second for Sub Pop, was co-produced with Jonathan Rado of Foxygen and swaps the sparser folk of her earlier records for lush, 1970s-FM-radio-styled orchestral pop, with songs circling climate anxiety and movie-fed romantic longing.
albums.reception: The album holds a Metacritic score of 91 out of 100 based on 26 critic reviews, a rating the site classifies as universal acclaim.

albums.blurb: Natalia Lafourcade is a singer-songwriter from Veracruz, Mexico, who moved from indie pop toward the Latin American folk songbook over the 2010s. Musas, Vol. 1, her sixth studio album, followed her 2015 breakthrough Hasta la Raíz and pairs her with Los Macorinos, the veteran acoustic guitar duo of Juan Carlos Allende and Miguel Peña best known for accompanying Chavela Vargas; it mixes new originals with covers drawn from composers like Agustín Lara and Violeta Parra.
albums.reception: It won Best Folk Album at the 18th Latin Grammy Awards in 2017, and Rolling Stone included it in its list of the ten best Latin albums of that year.
